title: Tunnel-auth route_hash: spec+Python hash full 16-byte hop addresses; Rust+C+committed vector hash 8-byte IIDs (spec 8.11)
description: spec/06-security.md §8.11 route-hash amendment (R-06-315): route_hash = SHA-256 over FULL 16-byte hop addresses in SRH visitation order, because under AddrForKey a 02xx address embeds no IID (slicing 8 bytes yields no identity meaning). Python conforms (python/src/lichen/gateway/tunnel_auth.py:155-163). Rust hashes 8-byte hops (rust/lichen-gateway/src/tunnel_auth.rs:493-503), C hashes 8-byte IIDs (lichen/subsys/lichen/gateway/tunnel_auth.c:201-216), and the committed vector pins the 8-byte form (test/vectors/tunnel_authorization.json:61-65 route_hops_hex 8-byte + route_hash_hex 2e7e354d...). Consequence: a Python-signed grant is unverifiable by a Rust/C egress and vice versa (interop break); also the 64-bit IID-collision false loop-rejection the spec amendment calls out remains in Rust/C. Fix: migrate Rust+C hash inputs to 16-byte reconstructed SRH hop addresses, regenerate test/vectors/tunnel_authorization.json (LICHEN-generated fixture, may change), update Rust/C tests (lichen/tests/tunnel_auth, tunnel_auth_vectors.rs). Suggested placement: rust/lichen-gateway/src/tunnel_auth.rs + lichen/subsys/lichen/gateway/tunnel_auth.c + test/vectors/tunnel_authorization.json.
